# C3 evaluation: simulated children, stress test and replay test

*Generated by `node src/modules/c3/evaluation/run.js` on 2026-10-20: 80 simulated children (half 5–10, half 11–14), 10 sessions of 25 minutes each, 10 seeds for the main comparisons. Each seed is a new cohort; all recommenders meet the same children on the same seed, so differences are paired. ± is a 95 % confidence interval over seeds.*

All numbers come from a **simulator**, not from children. They show how the recommenders behave under the stated assumptions (`evaluation/childModel.js`, A1–A6), and the stress test shows where that changes. They are not evidence of clinical benefit; the replay test on pilot sessions and the SLP check are the steps that bring real data in.

**Measures** (per activity, averaged over all activities):
- **Reward per activity:** the true expected 0.6 P + 0.4 E, the quantity the server's reward estimates.
- **Regret vs oracle:** how much reward was lost against the best activity for that child at that moment.
- **True engagement:** the simulated child's actual engagement, not the noisy estimate the recommender sees.
- **Ability gain:** growth in the simulated child's ability over all sessions (assumption A5).
- **Too hard / far too easy:** shares of activities with P < 0.3, or demand more than 0.3 below ability.

## Summary

- **Hybrid LinUCB vs the alternatives** (reward per activity, paired): +0.144 ± 0.009 vs random (10/10 seeds); +0.068 ± 0.008 vs rules (10/10 seeds); +0.039 ± 0.007 vs linucb learning from the parent tap (10/10 seeds); +0.022 ± 0.003 vs linucb per child, no sharing (10/10 seeds).
- **Sharing across children:** session-1 regret 0.101 with the shared model vs 0.195 per child; by the last session they are close (0.079 vs 0.075). Sharing matters most for new children.
- **Reward vs learning:** the reward favours activities the child can already do: ability gain 0.147 under Hybrid LinUCB vs 0.237 under rules and 0.191 under random, and only 0.070 for the reward-maximising oracle (assumption A5). See section 2.
- **Learning signal:** engagement + performance beats the parent tap (+0.039 ± 0.007) and engagement alone (+0.086 ± 0.007); against performance alone it is +0.009 ± 0.007, but performance alone gives the least engaged children (true engagement 0.438 vs 0.627).
- **Where it stops winning:** Hybrid LinUCB is no longer clearly better than the best simple baseline under: engagement model badly wrong 70 % (misleading).
- **Replay test:** in the simulator the doubly robust estimate of a random recommender was off by 0.000 on average (SNIPS 0.001), so the estimators are ready for pilot logs.

## 2. Learning-signal comparison

The same Hybrid LinUCB, learning from different signals (`C3_REWARD_MODE` on the server). The outcome is the same true reward for all rows, so a signal is better when it leads to better activities, not because it is easier to score highly on.

| Recommender | Reward per activity | Session 1 | Last 3 sessions | Regret vs oracle | True engagement | Ability gain | Too hard (P < 0.3) | Far too easy |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Parent tap only | 0.655 ± 0.013 | 0.634 | 0.670 | 0.133 | 0.616 | 0.168 | 6.6 % | 5.0 % |
| Engagement only | 0.607 ± 0.007 | 0.565 | 0.656 | 0.183 | 0.788 | 0.330 | 24.4 % | 2.0 % |
| Performance only | 0.684 ± 0.014 | 0.664 | 0.687 | 0.102 | 0.438 | 0.056 | 1.1 % | 35.4 % |
| **Engagement + performance (server default)** | 0.693 ± 0.013 | 0.671 | 0.707 | 0.091 | 0.627 | 0.147 | 6.2 % | 16.7 % |
| Challenge + engagement (not in the plan) | 0.658 ± 0.010 | 0.644 | 0.664 | 0.128 | 0.701 | 0.227 | 10.6 % | 5.4 % |

- Hybrid LinUCB, engagement + performance (server) − LinUCB learning from the parent tap (old app signal): **+0.039** (95 % CI ± 0.007; better on 10 of 10 seeds)
- Hybrid LinUCB, engagement + performance (server) − Engagement only: **+0.086** (95 % CI ± 0.007; better on 10 of 10 seeds)
- Hybrid LinUCB, engagement + performance (server) − Performance (successes ÷ targets) only: **+0.009** (95 % CI ± 0.007; better on 8 of 10 seeds)

**Note on "challenge + engagement":** this row is not in the plan. It rewards success near 70 % instead of 100 %. It is here because, under assumption A5 (children learn most just above their level), any reward that is mostly "successes ÷ targets" steers towards activities the child already masters: compare the ability gain of the oracle and the default reward with rules and random in section 1. Whether A5 holds for children who stutter is a question for the SLP, and it decides which reward to use.

## 4. Replay test, validated in the simulator

The server logs every decision with its propensity, and with `C3_EXPLORE_EPSILON` > 0 some picks are random. Here the simulator logs Hybrid LinUCB with ε = 0.3, then `evaluation/ope.js` estimates how other recommenders would have done on the same children from those logs alone. The true value is known in the simulator, so the estimators' bias can be measured before they are used on pilot logs.

| Target policy | True value on the logged children | IPS | SNIPS | DR | Effective sample size |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Uniform random | 0.541 | 0.542 (bias +0.001, RMSE 0.007) | 0.540 (bias -0.001, RMSE 0.005) | 0.540 (bias -0.000, RMSE 0.004) | 1834 of 5734 |
| Easy activities only | 0.677 | 0.681 (bias +0.004, RMSE 0.013) | 0.680 (bias +0.003, RMSE 0.006) | 0.680 (bias +0.003, RMSE 0.006) | 625 of 5734 |
| Greedy on a model fitted to the first half (second half only) | 0.745 | 0.722 (bias -0.023, RMSE 0.044) | 0.744 (bias -0.001, RMSE 0.009) | 0.743 (bias -0.002, RMSE 0.011) | 70 of 2867 |

On pilot sessions: set `C3_EXPLORE_EPSILON` (for example 0.2), save `GET /api/c3/reports/replay-log?limit=500` to a file, and run `node src/modules/c3/evaluation/ope.js replay-log.json`. Only decisions logged after the candidate set was added to the log (this version) can be used.

## Assumptions and limits

- The simulated child (A1–A6) is a set of stated guesses, not a fitted model; numbers are comparisons between recommenders, not predictions for real children.
- Activity content, durations and the arm pool come from the placeholder catalog. A real SLP-reviewed catalog may change the results.
- The engagement estimate is simulated as true engagement plus error; the real camera model's error on children is unknown until the pilot check (`GET /api/c3/reports/engagement-pilot-check`).
- The oracle maximises the reward, not learning; it is an upper bound for the reward only.
